Scholarly Database-Driven Topic Generation

Ensuring Originality and Academic Rigor in Dissertation Topic Selection

Scholarly Database-Driven Topic Generation

Choosing a dissertation topic is arguably the most important decision that Master’s and PhD students in the UK and U.S. face. Your choice of topic dictates the journey you embark upon during the dissertation process, and it can impact your academic success, publication potential, and your career opportunities. Utilizing scholarly database driven topic generation is one of the best ways to identify a unique, relevant, and rigorous dissertation topic

What is Scholarly Database-Driven Topic Generation?

Data-driven topic generation includes intentionally searching the literature for relevant, scholarly research across a variety of databases including ProQuest, JSTOR, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar. By reviewing the most recent studies, dissertations, and peer reviewed journal articles, you can explore research gaps, identify research trends, and ensure that your dissertation topics are original and worthy of research.

Why Use Scholarly Databases for Dissertation Topic Selection?

Access to Current and Authoritative Research

Databases offer high-impact, peer-reviewed sources that allow you to base your dissertation on the most reliable research to date.

Identification of Research Gaps

Literature reviews allow you to identify literary gaps and conflicting findings that can add to your original topic.

Compliance with Academic Standards

UK and US dissertation committees generally expect the topic you choose to be grounded in a comprehensive knowledge of the research that already exists. Generally, using databases means you will meet the requirements for your topic.

Interdisciplinary Topic Innovation

Searching across disciplines opens up potential for you to develop your topic at an innovative intersection of multiple disciplines.

Our Process for Database-Driven Topic Selection

StepDescription
1. Literature SearchSystematic review of literature databases, such as ProQuest, JSTOR, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar.
2. Research Gap AnalysisIdentifying contradictions, limitations, and unanswered questions in existing research.
3. Methodology AlignmentEnsuring categories are aligned with qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods scope and approach.
4. Detailed Topic OutlinesProviding research aims, objectives, and highlights of relevant literature. Including the approach or design and data analysis methods, if applicable.
This process provides students with a visual representation of the research journey and gets them normalised to submission of proposals.

Practical Tips for Effective Use of Scholarly Databases

  • Use precise keywords and Boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT) to focus searches.
  • Try not to go beyond five years for new publications.
  • You can quickly determine relevance by reading abstract and conclusions.
  • Review not just sources but your own citations and references for sources to support additional sources.
  • Use the filters that are available; Publication/type, date and subject.

    • Benefits of Choosing Database-Driven Topics

  • Enhances Research credibility: Getting approval on topics stemming from peer-reviewed literature has immediate approval.
  • Increases likelihood of publication: If you can identify a research gap, the likelihood of being accepted into a journal improves.
  • Redundancy: Saves everyone time and resources if there is no duplication.
  • Supports Interdisciplinary investigation: Provides for innovative means of creating combinations instead of subject.
